analysis.title: Microchip Technology Inc. (MCHP): First Take: Solid quarter, but weaker guidance
key_insights: GS expects MCHP to trade lower after a solid FY2Q27 quarter and below-Street FY3Q27 guidance. Expectations were somewhat elevated going into the print because of strong margin guidance, management commentary on signs of restocking, and solid results from analog peers.

FY2Q27 results were in line with the Street: revenue $1.62 bn vs GS $1.62 bn and Street $1.61 bn, gross margin 66.5% vs 66.6% for both GS and Street, operating margin 39.5% vs GS 39.3% and Street 39.1%, and EPS $0.97 vs GS $0.96 and Street $0.94.

FY3Q27 guidance midpoint is below the Street on every line: revenue $1.61 bn vs GS $1.65 bn and Street $1.63 bn, non-GAAP gross margin 64.5% vs GS 66.2% and Street 66.5%, non-GAAP operating margin 37.8% vs GS 39.4% and Street 39.0%, and non-GAAP EPS $0.91 vs GS $0.98 and Street $0.95.

Guided gross margin of 64.5% is about 173 bps below GS and 196 bps below the Street, the largest gap among the guided lines. The call is expected to focus on gross margin trajectory and the net effect of higher input costs and ASPs.
GS expects the call to focus on three topics: datacenter exposure and outlook given the new narrative, demand trends and share dynamics in non-AI-related end markets, and gross margin trajectory.

GS sees a limited negative read-across for the analog group because most peers have already reported. The most direct read-across is for TXN (Sell) and ADI (Buy) because of their relatively high industrial exposures.

GS keeps a Buy rating and a $115 12-month target price on MCHP, based on 26X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $4.50. The target implies 52.6% upside from $75.34. Key risks are the timing of the analog and MCU recovery, and inventory on the balance sheet delaying margin expansion relative to peers.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $115 target after the print despite expecting the stock to trade lower on below-Street FY3Q27 guidance. The target rests on 26X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $4.50.
GS expects TXN to see the most direct negative read-across from MCHP's weaker guidance because of its relatively high industrial exposure.
GS expects ADI to see the most direct negative read-across from MCHP's weaker guidance because of its relatively high industrial exposure.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees a limited negative read-across from MCHP's guidance because most analog peers have already reported.

earnings_insights: MCHP FY2Q27 reported (non-GAAP, excl. SBC): revenue $1,622 mn vs GS $1,617 mn and Street $1,608 mn (Visible Alpha). Revenue up 9.2% QoQ and 42.2% YoY.
MCHP FY2Q27 reported (excl. SBC): gross margin 66.5% vs GS 66.6% and Street 66.6%. Operating margin 39.5% vs GS 39.3% and Street 39.1%. EPS $0.97 vs GS $0.96 and Street $0.94.

MCHP FY3Q27 guidance (company guide, excl. SBC): revenue midpoint $1,606 mn (range $1,573 mn to $1,638 mn) vs GS estimate $1,648 mn and Street estimate $1,628 mn. Midpoint implies -1.0% QoQ and +35.4% YoY.

MCHP FY3Q27 guidance (excl. SBC): gross margin midpoint 64.5% (range 64.0% to 65.0%) vs GS estimate 66.2% and Street estimate 66.5%. Operating margin midpoint 37.8% (range 37.0% to 38.5%) vs GS estimate 39.4% and Street estimate 39.0%.
MCHP FY3Q27 guidance (excl. SBC): EPS midpoint $0.91 (range $0.87 to $0.95) vs GS estimate $0.98 and Street estimate $0.95, which is 7.0% below GS and 4.3% below the Street.
GS quarterly EPS estimates (excl. SBC): $0.63 for the June 2026 quarter, $0.83 for Sep 2026E, $0.85 for Dec 2026E and $0.92 for Mar 2027E. GS FY3/27E EPS is $3.23 and FY3/28E is $4.28.
risk_factors: Timing of the analog and MCU recovery.
Inventory on the balance sheet could delay the company's margin expansion relative to peers.
Higher input costs and ASPs may have a net effect on gross margin that is unclear, which GS flags as a call focus.

tension_points.bull_case: Quarter was in line to slightly ahead of the Street, and GS keeps a Buy with a $115 target (52.6% upside) on 26X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $4.50. Management had earlier cited signs of a restocking dynamic.
tension_points.bear_case: FY3Q27 guidance is below the Street on revenue, gross margin, operating margin and EPS after expectations had risen on strong margin guidance and solid analog peer results. GS expects the stock to trade lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names the timing of the analog and MCU recovery, and inventory on the balance sheet delaying margin expansion relative to peers, as key risks to the thesis.
